messages.subject: Issues with as.telemetry() from move object
parts:
We are working with a large multi-year data set of GPS relocations of tortoises. My current issue is coercing our data into a telemetry object from a move object. I can make the move object for an individual animal with no issue, but when I use "as.telemetry" to coerce into a telemetry object I get thousands of lines that say "Minimum sampling interval of Inf years in XXXXX" and warnings:
"1: In Move2CSV(object, timeformat = timeformat, timezone = timezone,  ... :Move objects in geographic coordinates are automatically projected."
and "In min(dt) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf"
 and the resulting object can't used in any further functions.

This is the code I am using (allgps is a SpatialPointsDataFrame pulled from our Postgres server):

allgps$DateTime <- as.POSIXct(allgps$DateTime, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

allgps.df <- as.data.frame(allgps)

CN802.a<-allgps.df[allgps.df$Tort == "CN802",]
CN802.a <- CN802.a[order(CN802.a$DateTime),]

CN802.a.m <- move(x=CN802.a$x, y=CN802.a$y,time=CN802.a$DateTime, data=CN802.a, proj=proj4string(allgps),sensor="gps", animal=CN802.a$Tort)
CN802.a.t <- as.telemetry(CN802.a.m, timeformat="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", timezone= "America/Los_Angeles",timeout=Inf,na.rm="row", drop=TRUE)

What's strange is that my colleague also used this same code to get a subset of this data to work fine, the only differences I can find between our approaches is that she started from a .csv which she had edited in Excel, but I can't find any differences between the structure of her move object and mine.


I found that can run the move object through the functions here: https://rpubs.com/dracodoc/252699
and get a telemetry object, though I then get errors about UERE missing when I try to go use ctmm.fit()

I'm assuming it has something to do with POSIX formatting, but I am at a bit of a loss now,

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Issues with as.telemetry() from move object
parts:
Hi Steve,

This sounds like problems with the timestamp format or timezone. I can point out a couple of things:

  1. You could be feeding in different timestamps into move() and as.telemetry(). For move() you did not supply a timezone argument in as.POSIXct(), which means that the (default) local timezone of your computer was used. Yet for as.telemetry(), you supplied the timezone of "America/Los_Angeles". I would also note, that most collars/tags are UTC, to avoid timezone issues, and not the timezone of the study area.
  2. When you open and re-save a CSV file in Excel, it can reformat your timestamps. Usually this is a danger because it can corrupt your data, but in this case it could have served to fix or better standardize your timestamps.
If that doesn't fix your problems, then you can feel free to send me some sample data to replicate the issue and I can take a look.

Best,
Chris

Hi Lucy,

I think the projection errors are from the BNG locations being imported as long-lat. as.telemetry() assumes MoveBank format with long-lat in appropriately named columns, and you can specify the projection you want to work in on or after import.

Chris
